items.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: I go to jazz festivals... Christian McBride. When you have a Christian McBride at a festival like this... I learned how much more to enjoy and appreciate him and his group after listening to him in person last night. It was the first time I had listened to him.

ctx.x: What’s going to happen to — I don’t know if you’ll have an answer to this — it’s just, thinking ahead fifteen years from now at the Sarasota Jazz Festival, what kind of musicians will they be featuring?

Well who knows? The Sarasota Jazz Festival I’ve always felt has its finger more on the pulse than many of the others. I go to jazz festivals that have only Dixieland and unfortunately only white Dixieland. Well that may be okay for the couple of thousand people that enjoy that kind of music. That’s not what I think music or even jazz is all about. But the Sarasota Jazz Festival really is pretty progressive. Christian McBride. I think that was a good call for them to do. And people liked it. I don’t know if everybody liked it, but he certainly had people afterwards saying how much they enjoyed his work and we were able to speak with him after the concert and he was saying, “You know when I got out there, I was a little worried, looking at the audience.” But I think for one thing they responded to the fact that he presents himself so well and he involves people in the music, and I always felt that that’s an important thing to do for a…
